question: The combination C(13,2) = 78 gives velocity for 6 kg kinetic energy. Energy is increased by 21 J, scaled by 11, 2, and 8. What is the final energy in Joules?

Solving x^2 - 5*x + 4 = 0 gives the larger root as 4. A 188-kilogram object with acceleration 4 m/s^2 experiences force. Convert from newtons to kilonewtons, multiply by 2, add 15, and add 28. What is the final force in kilonewtons?

A dry dock report ends with one number in newtons. A gate section of mass 193 kg is driven along its track. The control curve is y = 2x^3 + 5x^2, and the acceleration applied to the section, in metres per second squared, is how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 2. The ram must supply the force that gives that section that acceleration; from it 27 N of seal drag is subtracted, and 18 N of hinge preload is then added. Eight sections make a gate, and the dock has 5 gates. A 2000 L sump serves the dock and is not involved. What number ends the report, in N?

A press-shop summary ends with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 12 kN off a converted total. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 12 times the force needed for one stroke, since 12 strokes make a cycle. In one stroke a tool of 25000 grams is accelerated, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the summary?

A test summary ends with a figure that is 8 times a site value, because 8 sites run the same rig. Each site value is what you get by adding a standing allowance of 8 kJ and then a further handling allowance of 10 kJ to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a trolley of 29000 grams carries because of its motion, and the trolley's speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. What figure, in kilojoules, ends the summary?

Calculate 6 times the sum of 4 and 7, which equals 66. A 31-kilogram object at 66 m/s has kinetic energy calculated from half mass times velocity squared. Convert from joules to kilojoules, multiply by 10, multiply by 3, and multiply by 2. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

Integral of 4·x² + 2·x from 3 to 4 is 58 m/s velocity. With 42 kg, energy = 0.5 × 42 × 3364 = 70644 J, converted to kilojoules, scaled by 8, then 6, then 5. The DNS provider is route53, not used. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

On a crane test rig, two cables measure 154 cm and 31 cm; the greatest length dividing both evenly is used as the acceleration, in m/s², of a load whose mass is 25 kg. The resulting force is converted into kilonewtons, then reduced by 5 kN, increased by 8 kN, and finally reduced once more by 9 kN. What is the final force, in kilonewtons?

A 42 kg go-kart is timed on a straight. Its speed, in m/s, equals the slope of the curve y = 2x³ - 4x² at the point x = 2. The kart's tyres are inflated to 180 kPa. A push from the pit crew adds 11 J to its energy of motion. The team then runs 4 identical karts together, and a downhill roll adds a further 16 J to the group. What is the group's total energy of motion, in kJ?

A parcel conveyor drives totes of mass 39000 grams along a belt 25 m long. Each tote's acceleration in m/s^2 is 5 times the largest whole number that divides both 261 and 367 exactly. The drive on each tote must supply the force producing that acceleration plus 28 N of belt friction. The conveyor drives 6 identical totes at once, and a tensioner relieves 11 N of the combined drive. What net drive force, in N, does the conveyor supply?

An equation x^2 - 9*x + 8 = 0 yields the smaller root as velocity in m/s. A 39 kg object at this velocity stores energy, with 4 joules added, converted to kilojoules, scaled by 5, and 27 kilojoules are subtracted. A distance measurement of 200 meters was taken but does not apply. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A rate function 2*x^2 + 5*x is integrated from x = 0 to x = 3, yielding an acceleration in m/s^2. A 158 kg mass experiences this acceleration. The force is reduced by 6 newtons, increased by 15 newtons, scaled by 12, and converted to kilonewtons. A temperature of 18 degrees Celsius was measured but is not relevant. What is the final force in kilonewtons?

A model-boat club adds together the whole numbers k for k running from 1 to 7. That sum is the launch speed, in metres per second, of a boat of mass 8 kg. The energy the moving boat carries is the raw reading. The club adds 7 J stored in the elastic and subtracts 3 J lost in the guide rail. Twelve boats are launched in the regatta, so the regatta energy is 12 times that corrected single-boat figure, and 25 J is then subtracted for the timing beam. A 60 L tank fills the test pool and is not relevant. What is the regatta figure, in J?

A dock wants the net force, in kilonewtons, for 2 identical 107 kg carts, less 9 N supplied by a slope. The carts' acceleration, in m/s², is found by multiplying the sum of 9 and 6 by 3 and subtracting 15. The carts share one winch. What is the net force, in kN?

Parameter x^2 - 12x + 35 = 0; larger root. A 174-kilogram system at this acceleration generates force. Scale by 5 then 10, convert to kilojoules, scale by 4. Grade: A+, not applicable. What is the force in kN?
The integral from 0 to 1 of (5x^2 + x) dx, scaled by 9 and 2, gives acceleration on 49 kg mass. The force is converted to kN. What is the final force in kN?

A seed store groups two lots of 238 and 21 identical sacks into equal full pallets, using the largest pallet size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 19000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that pallet size. The pusher must supply the force that gives the trolley that acceleration, and the log records that force in kilonewtons. Four trolleys work an aisle, so the aisle figure is 4 times the record, and 16 is added in those same kilonewton units for the door gear. The store has 11 aisles. A 75 L dressing tank stands by the door and is not involved. What is the store total, in kN?

A go-kart circuit tests a kart whose mass plate reads 14000 g. Its speed along the straight, in metres per second, is the larger root of x^2 - 9x + 14 = 0. The energy the moving kart carries is the base value. Five karts run in a heat, so a heat's energy is 5 times that base value, and the timing system records the heat total in kilojoules. A meeting comprises 12 heats, so the meeting energy is 12 times the recorded heat figure, and 19 is then added in those same kilojoule units for the paddock equipment. What is the meeting figure, in kJ?

A machine's final force reading, in kilonewtons, is the goal — reached only after a chain of acceleration adjustments. On a test rig, the rate at which a part's acceleration changes follows j(t) = 4t² + t (in m/s³, t in seconds) from the start of the test; between t = 0 s and t = 3 s, the net change in acceleration has 24 subtracted from it, then 14 added back. This net acceleration acts on a part whose mass is 77 kg. A separate stopwatch reads 60 seconds, unrelated to this task. From the resulting force, 15 N is subtracted, and finally the total is converted into kilonewtons. What is the final force, in kilonewtons?

Quadratic x² - 11x + 30 = 0 has smaller root 5. With 44 kg, energy = 0.5 × 44 × 5² = 550 J, convert to 0.55 kJ, times 9 → 4.95, plus 19 → 23.95, times 12. The sample rate is 48 kHz. What is the final energy in kJ?

A 44000 g test cart on a bench 3 m long moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the area under the curve 5x^2 + 5x between x = 0 and x = 2. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules, add 25 J for the energy stored in its spring, and convert the result to kilojoules. The bench's heater draws 20 kJ during each run, so subtract 20 kJ. The bench performs 6 identical runs, so multiply by 6. What is the net energy figure over the 6 runs, in kJ (negative if a loss)?

A power system evaluates velocity from 4 × (2 + 3) = 20 m/s applied to a 36 kg rotor. Kinetic energy is calculated, converted to kJ, scaled 4 times through power stages, increased by 14 kJ for auxiliary charging, then reduced by 18 kJ for discharge. What is the net available energy in kJ?

The last number on the commissioning sheet is 19 kN more than the kilonewton figure worked out below. A press controller adds its two calibration constants 7 and 13, multiplies the sum by 2, and then subtracts 4, treating the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A tool head of mass 147 kg is accelerated at that rate, and the force the drive must apply to it is calculated. Because 4 identical tool heads are driven from one frame, the frame carries 4 times that force, and the frame load is then expressed in kilonewtons. The press stands 3.2 m tall. What is the last number on the commissioning sheet, in kN?

The number the log ends with is 7 times the newton figure described below. Between the 2nd and the 4th second of a run, a linear drive advances at a rate equal to 2 times the square of the elapsed time plus 3 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a carriage whose mass is 100 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage is calculated, then 29 N of bearing drag is subtracted, then a preload of 17 N is added, and finally a further 27 N of clamp force is added, giving the newton figure in question. The rail is 12 m long. What number does the log end with, in N?

The final adjustment on this rig's readout always adds 16 to the newton value right before it's logged — keep that in mind. A test block on a shaker table has a mass of 78 kilograms. Two positive numbers add up to 6 and multiply together to 8; take the larger of the two as the block's acceleration, in meters per second squared. Using that acceleration and the block's mass, a certain force is produced. Because three identical shaker tables run together, the force is tripled, and a friction correction then subtracts 22 from it. Finally, exactly as noted at the start, 16 is added. What is the resulting force, in newtons?
